meta.title: The Present Subjunctive: Uses
meta.subtitle: Wishes, emotions, doubt, impersonal expressions, ojalá and the main conjunctions
meta.footer: Spanish Learning Program · B1 · Grammar · Subjunctive uses

blocks.title: After this PDF you can
bullets: decide when a clause after que needs the subjunctive
use it after wishes, emotions, doubt, impersonal expressions and ojalá
contrast it with the indicative (creo que viene / no creo que venga)
use it after para que, antes de que, sin que, and with cuando for the future

blocks.text: The subjunctive appears in a subordinate clause introduced by que when the main clause expresses something other than a plain fact. A short memory aid is WEIRDO:

head: Letter
Trigger
Example
rows: Me alegro de que estés aquí.

blocks.title: Two conditions must be true
bullets: The two clauses have different subjects: Quiero que tú vengas. With the same subject use the infinitive: Quiero venir.
The main clause expresses influence, feeling or doubt, not certainty: Sé que vienes (indicative) vs Dudo que vengas (subjunctive).

head: Verb
Example
English
rows: I want you to help me.
I ask you to listen to me.
I need you to come soon.
Te recomiendo que pruebes el pescado.
I recommend that you try the fish.
No me deja que salga tarde.
He doesn't let me go out late.
My parents forbid me to smoke.

blocks.title: decir que: fact or order?
blocks.text: Dice que viene (he says he is coming) gives information: indicative. Dice que vengas (he tells you to come) gives an order: subjunctive. The same applies to escribir que and gritar que.

blocks.title: Dutch dat = que + subjunctive
blocks.text: Ik hoop dat je komt is Espero que vengas; Ik wil dat je helpt is Quiero que ayudes. In Dutch the verb after dat is in the normal present, in Spanish it is not.

head: Expression
Example
English
rows: alegrarse de que / me alegra que
I am glad you are better.
I love it that you cook.
It bothers me that you arrive late.
Me sorprende que no sepa nada.
It surprises me that he knows nothing.
I am afraid it will rain.
I am sorry you can't come.
Es una pena que se vayan.
It is a pity that they are leaving.

items: After verbs and expressions with de (alegrarse de, tener miedo de, estar contento de) keep the preposition before que: Me alegro de que vengas.

head: Subjunctive (doubt, denial)
Indicative (certainty)
English
rows: I don't think he is coming. / I think he is coming.
I doubt he is right. / I don't doubt he is right.
No es verdad que sea fácil.
It isn't true that it is easy. / It is true that it is easy.
No estoy seguro de que funcione.
I'm not sure it works. / I'm sure it works.
I deny he knows. / It is obvious he knows.

head: Expression of possibility
Mood
Example
rows: es posible que, es probable que, puede ser que

blocks.title: Question: is it a fact or an opinion?
blocks.text: Creer, pensar, opinar, parecer and estar seguro take the indicative when affirmative (they state belief as fact) and the subjunctive when negative. In a question the choice depends on the doubt: ¿Crees que viene? (neutral) vs ¿Crees que venga? (you doubt it).

head: Subjunctive
Example
English
rows: It is necessary that you arrive soon.
It is better that we wait.
Es una lástima que no vengas.
It is a pity that you don't come.
It is strange that he doesn't answer.

head: Indicative (certainty)
Example
English
rows: es verdad / cierto / obvio / evidente que
It is obvious that he is right.
It is clear that he is not coming.

items: General statements use the infinitive (no subject): Es importante estudiar. A specific person needs que + subjunctive: Es importante que tú estudies.

head: Expression
Example
English
rows: I hope the weather is good.
I hope it goes well for you!

blocks.text: Ojalá comes from Arabic inshallah and works without a subject: Ojalá vengas. Ojalá lo sepa.

head: Always subjunctive
English
Example
rows: Te lo explico para que lo entiendas.
Iré con tal de que vengas.
Lleva paraguas en caso de que llueva.

head: Time and concession
Future / unknown: subjunctive
Habit / fact: indicative
rows: En cuanto lo sepa, te aviso.
En cuanto lo sé, te aviso.
Aunque llueva, iré. (even if it rains)
Aunque llueve, voy. (although it is raining)

blocks.title: Dutch present for the future
blocks.text: Dutch says Als je aankomt, bel me and Wanneer ik aankom, bel ik with the same present tense. Spanish distinguishes: Cuando llegues (it has not happened yet) vs Cuando llego (it happens regularly).

rows: Same subject: infinitive instead of que.
Affirmative creer que takes the indicative.
Negative creer que takes the subjunctive.
es verdad que states a fact: indicative.
cuando + future meaning needs the subjunctive.
Te lo digo para que sabes.
Te lo digo para que sepas.
para que is always followed by the subjunctive.
a lo mejor takes the indicative.
Keep de before que, and use the subjunctive.

blocks.text: Write the verb in brackets in the subjunctive, the indicative or the infinitive. Answers are on the last page.

items.q: Quiero que tú ______ a la fiesta.
items.full: Quiero que tú vengas a la fiesta.

items.q: Es importante que ellos ______ la verdad.
items.full: Es importante que ellos sepan la verdad.
Me alegro de que estés bien.

items.q: No creo que el examen ______ difícil.
items.full: No creo que el examen sea difícil.

items.q: Te lo explico para que lo ______.
items.full: Te lo explico para que lo entiendas.

items.q: Cuando ______ a casa mañana, te llamaré.
items.full: Cuando llegue a casa mañana, te llamaré.

items.q: Voy a esperar hasta que tú ______.
items.full: Voy a esperar hasta que tú vuelvas.
Es verdad que ellos están cansados.

items.q: I hope you have a nice weekend.
items.a: Espero que tengas un buen fin de semana.

items.q: I don't think he is coming.
